fixes.explanation: Nobody gets walked to the border here. The text says Abimelech had Sarah brought to him (Genesis 20:2), so the king's move is about Sarah, not Abraham's exit. I think Abraham is standing there holding his breath. And a dream is headed the king's way that very night (Genesis 20:3).

Loyalty is the word, baker. Abraham tells the king what he asked of Sarah: “This is how you can show your loyalty to me…” (Genesis 20:13) He's explaining himself after the fact, and he ties it back to when God had him journey from his father's house. Explaining yourself after the fact is a skill I know well, friend. I've done it over a tray of crumbs.

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The explanation says Abimelech has no idea what is coming, but the passage does not say what he knows or expects before the dream.
